annotations.title: Holdings of an investor, fund or person

description: Returns what investors hold in the tracked AI and semiconductor companies, from SEC filings. With `holder` (a key, a name such as 'Vanguard', or the `holder` value of get_ownership, get_insider_trading or get_fund_flows): one holder in detail — positions by company with their move and `heldSince`, sectors, flows, Schedule 13D/G declarations, `history` since the end of 2019, `performance` of its declared picks with its rank, and `follow` (its page and an Atom feed); for a person, each stake broken down (`breakdown`: shares held, restricted shares, options) with their roles and Forms 3, 4 and 5. Without `holder`, a ranked `list`: the largest holders (default), companies that invest in others, buyers, sellers, 13D/G declarants, individuals, or the best-performing active managers over `period`. Use it when the user asks what a fund, an investor or a person owns, or who bought, sold or performed most. A person has two figures for one company — shares held (Form 4) and beneficial ownership (Schedule 13D/G, options and unvested shares included): say which one you quote. `performance` measures declared picks, not a fund's return. `coverage.complete` false means the figures are a floor.

holder.description: For one holder's detail: its key from a list (vanguard, blackrock, nvidia), a name ('BlackRock', 'Vanguard', or a person's name), or the `holder` value another tool returned (for a director, their name and a ticker, e.g. 'Larry Ellison (ORCL)').

list.description: Without `holder`: 'largest' (default), 'investors' (universe companies filing 13F), 'buyers' or 'sellers' (by net move), 'declarants' (Schedule 13D/G holders filing no 13F), 'individuals' (people, from their 13D/G), 'performance' (active managers ranked by the return of their declared AI-stock portfolio).

order.description: With list 'performance': 'best' (default: highest return first) or 'worst' (lowest first).

period.description: With list 'performance': 'quarter' (default: the last completed quarter), 'year', '3y' or '5y' — quarterly returns chained.
